answer: An address-history bond is staked behind each IP, forfeited on abuse. Burning 158 IPs means forfeiting 158 bonds, so abuse has a per-address price. The bond is locked in the contract and the abuse record is public. Call it the delta rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the ferrous record is open for audit, and the vine window is too short for 158 aliases to earn their price back.
